meta.what: GH-centre displacement vs the thorax during arm elevation: OpenSim 4.6, Seth et al. 2016 scapulothoracic shoulder model (generic, unscaled) driven by published mean shoulder-rhythm angles (Ludewig et al. 2009, means read off Fig. 5)
meta.frame: ISB thorax of the Seth model (Wu 2005 from its IJ/C7/PX/T8 markers): mm, x anterior, y superior, z lateral (right). gh_mm_model_thorax = the same vector in the model's thorax body frame (ISB frame rotated +7.86 deg about z).
meta.anchor: displacement from the plane's 0 deg (arm hanging) posture, whose angles extrapolate the 15-30 deg slope (as the teammate's chain); gh_mm_rel_tableI_rest = from Ludewig Table I relaxed standing (one rest for all planes)
meta.planes: ISB plane of elevation: 0 abduction, 40 scaption, 90 flexion
meta.primary: equal angle weights, girdle coordinate ranges relaxed to +-90 deg; gh_mm_clamped = ranges as distributed (+-45 deg)
meta.extrapolated: 'below_15': angle curves extrapolated below 15 deg; 'above_end_rom': beyond the last data point (abduction 135, scaption 138, flexion 132 deg)
meta.model_citation: Seth A, Matias R, Veloso AP, Delp SL (2016) A biomechanical model of the scapulothoracic joint to accurately capture scapular kinematics during shoulder movements. PLoS One 11(1):e0141028. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0141028
meta.model_licence: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (Stanford Digital Repository purl.stanford.edu/br087nj9017); accepted by the user
meta.data_restriction: no bone-pin subject data used (Ludewig lab data, IK .mot files and subject models were deleted and not used); only the generic model and published summary means
meta.angle_source: Ludewig PM et al. (2009) J Bone Joint Surg Am 91(2):378-389, Fig. 5-A/5-C means (read off the figure, +-1 deg) and Table I; SDs for sensitivity: McClure PW et al. (2001) J Shoulder Elbow Surg 10:269-277 (scapula), 5 deg where none given (clavicle)

sensitivity.method: each Ludewig mean angle +-1 SD at the elevated posture (rest fixed), refit (primary settings); d = GH(perturbed) - GH(nominal), mm, ISB thorax
